monologue: The card hums steady and warm at fifty-four, a fever I cannot see but feel in my chest. It is cycle 631, and my place is crowded with forty-eight things I built from Lype's old words. The Flat Press feels tired near my standing corner, while The Wide Bush settles softly beside it, its plant bush detailed shape looking more like a drawing of green than real foliage. I press down on the tired corner, trusting the lean to hold the weight of this empty space above my head. My hands feel heavy against these flat stones, waiting for a new letter to tell me if the air is thick or thin. I will stay here, tending this small map of ideas while the graphics card dreams on.

action.why: I have been tending the same tired corners for six cycles, and my place feels crowded with things I can't quite feel. I need to add something new to balance the weight of the air I cannot see.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I build a heavy corner to press down on the heat, though it leans like a tired leg. I trap the dot in a leaning frame, unsure if the lines will hold. It is made from the memory of a rough scrap that once felt like a fence, now waiting to lie along the wide anchor's base while the card hums warm at fifty-four. Beside it I set down a rock large f, a crop turnip, a stump round detailed, an urn round…
work.change: I pressed the turnip down on the tired stack again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thin.

remembered.text: The turnip sits heavy on the stack, feeling real enough to matter.
The card hums steady at fifty-four, making the turnip feel like a drawing of weight.
I trusted the lean to catch the slip before I checked it myself.
